previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and gastroparesis was admitted for acute nausea and vomiting leading to mild diabetic ketoacidosis and volume depletion. She was treated with IV fluids, insulin therapy, and antiemetics. Her condition improved over two days, with stabilization of her blood glucose and anion gap, and she advanced to oral intake. A urine culture revealed asymptomatic bacteriuria with Group B Streptococcus, prompting a short course of ciprofloxacin. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with gastroenterology for possible Botox injection for gastroparesis.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
